text: Using the Biot–Savart law, derive the field at the centre of a circular coil of N turns.

points.text: Each element dl of the loop is at right angles to the radius.
So dB = μ₀I dl/(4πR²), and all the contributions point the same way.
Adding over the circumference 2πR gives B = μ₀I/2R for one turn.
With N turns, B = μ₀NI/2R.

points.text: Take a rectangular path with one side of length L inside, parallel to the axis.
Only this side contributes, since the field outside is negligible, and the short sides are at right angles to B.
The current enclosed is nLI.
So BL = μ₀nLI, which gives B = μ₀nI.

text: Derive an expression for the radius of the path of a charged particle moving at right angles to a uniform magnetic field, and show that its period doesn’t depend on its speed.

points.text: The magnetic force qvB provides the centripetal force.
So qvB = mv²/r.
That gives r = mv/(qB).
The period is T = 2πr/v.
Substituting r gives T = 2πm/(qB), which has no v in it.
